metadata.note: The Cambria and Indiana Railroad (chartered 1904 as the Blacklick and Yellow Creek, a Vinton Lumber Co. logging road; renamed 20 April 1911), a Cambria/Indiana County, Pennsylvania coal road best known for freight, which also ran scheduled passenger service by mixed trains and its own motor cars (the "Stump Dodger") on Colver - Rexis, and in 1916 on Colver - Manver. Two features, drawn only for confirmed years: Colver - Rexis 1914-1925 and Colver - Manver 1916 [ANCHOR]. The work-queue note "freight; do not add" is right for 1932-1994 but wrong for the 1910s-1920s. Research report: research/branches/cambria_and_indiana_railroad.txt.

metadata.ownership_split: None. 1922: Coleman's 40% sold to the NYC's Clearfield Bituminous Coal Co. - a stock holding, not an operator change (the AP 1924 story's "subsidiary of the New York Central" reflects it). 1950 Bethlehem Steel majority is post-passenger. The C&I ran its own trains throughout.
metadata.freight_only: Excluded under Rule 1 (report RULE NOTES): the Feb 1952 Official Guide (entry dated Aug 1951) lists the whole C&I as "Operated for Freight Service Only" and daggers every C&I station. Not drawn: [4] Revloc - Mine 33 / Cambria Slope (built 1963, coal only); [5] Nanty Glo mine branch and Springfield Branch; [6] Blacklick Secondary Ebensburg Jct - Nanty Glo (acquired 1998); [7] all freight years 1932-1994 on the main line and 1932-1977 on the Rexis Branch.
metadata.omitted: Report blocks not drawn, per their drawable: NONE: [3] Nanty Glo / Cambria Branch Regan Jct - Nanty Glo - Revloc (no confirmable passenger year; CamTran 1914 conflicts with trainweb's 1916 construction; Weber's 1931 mail-contract remark is the only hint); [8] Blacklick and Yellow Creek era Rexis - Stiles 1904-1910 (no passenger evidence); [9] "as needed" motor-car runs Dec 1931 - late 1930s (undated, and depends on the unconfirmed 1931 end). Blocks [4]-[7] are freight-only (see freight_only).

not_yet_sourced: Colver - Rexis END YEAR: 31 May 1925 (CamTran) vs 1 Dec 1931 (Weber, Delano's Domain; trainweb from Suiters/Hamley; en.wikipedia; american-rails). Drawn to 1925, the earlier. A primary source (Johnstown Tribune or Ebensburg Mountaineer-Herald for June 1925 and Nov-Dec 1931; PA Public Service Commission discontinuance order) would settle it; if 1931 is confirmed, extend to 1914-1931.

Colver - Rexis START YEAR: 1911 (CamTran) vs 1912 (CPTDB) vs 1914 (en.wikipedia, american-rails). Drawn from 1914; first primary-derived year is 1916. An ICC valuation report would give an operating date.
Colver - Manver: only 1916 is proven (Fowler 1916t) - [ANCHOR]. Start (c.1911-1912 per trainweb) and end are undated.
Nanty Glo / Revloc branch passenger service: no confirmable year; not drawn.
Post-1931 "as needed" motor-car runs: undated; not drawn.

Colver - Regan Jct on abandoned C&I-tagged grade (ways 12076864, 831255004, 711180446); Regan Jct - Elkdale Jct on the Ghost Town Trail - Stritty's Way (C&I-tagged cycleway). Elkdale Jct - Rexis: 0.06 mi on the C&I-tagged trail west of the Elkdale Jct node, 0.43 mi on OpenHistoricalMap way -202323441 ("Cambria and Indiana Railroad", 1904-1980) for the wye leg the OSM C&I ways do not carry, then the C&I-tagged "Rexis Branch" cycleway (ways 364273540, 364273541, 170535386) to its south end at Rexis. properties.geometry_quality: Traced 9.60 mi against 9.8 mi documented Colver - Rexis (1942 C&I employee timetable: Colver - Elkdale Jct 5.3 + Elkdale Jct - Rexis 4.5; Fowler tables 374/376 agree). Made of: Colver - Elkdale Jct 5.42 mi (doc 5.3; Colver - Regan Jct part 3.3 mi, matching the 1951 Official Guide's "Regan Junction to Colver (3.3 miles)") on C&I-tagged OSM grade/trail; Elkdale Jct - Rexis 4.18 mi (doc 4.5) of which 0.43 mi is the OpenHistoricalMap wye leg and the rest C&I-tagged OSM trail. No straight-line legs. Endpoints: Colver is the east end of the C&I-tagged grade (40.5424,-78.8012), 1.1 km west of the OSM Colver hamlet node - placed there because it reproduces the documented 3.3 mi to Regan Jct; Colver Heights (Fowler's zero, 2.2 mi further) is not drawn. Rexis is the south end of the Rexis Branch trail, 60 m from the OSM Rexis place node. The c.0.3 mi shortfall on Elkdale - Rexis is probably the wye geometry and the trail's end short of the PRR connection track; not resolved. LATER-ALIGNMENT NOTE: the drawn line is the grade as abandoned (Rexis Branch 1977, main line 1994-95) now carried by the Ghost Town Trail; no realignment between 1914 and abandonment is known, but none was checked against an era map.

segments.note: Scheduled passenger service Colver - Regan Jct - Dobson (later Elkdale) Jct - Rexis, the "Stump Dodger": mixed trains at first, then Brill battery cars (#14 received 1914, #15 1916 or 1917), replaced in 1922 by gasoline cars 98 and 99 (Service Motor Truck Co. with Brill bodies); the battery cars went to Canadian National in 1923. Carried US Mail. START 1914 is the latest of three secondary start claims (CamTran 1911, CPTDB 1912, en.wikipedia/american-rails 1914), all of which agree trains ran by 1914; trainweb (citing Suiters and Hamley) dates battery car #14 to 1914. The first PRIMARY-derived year is 1916: Fowler table 374/376 letters every Colver Heights - Manver and Dobson Jct - Rexis station "a" = a 1916 company public timetable. 1924 is primary-confirmed: the Associated Press story of 11 Oct 1924 (Evening Star p.1; Montgomery Advertiser 12 Oct p.28) has five bandits board "a gasoline-propelled combination coach" at Rexis and take seats behind the payroll messengers. END 1925 IS A SOURCE CONFLICT, drawn at the conservative end: CamTran says service was discontinued 31 May 1925 when the Brill car met a steam locomotive head on (an account with demonstrable errors - it calls the car overhead-powered), while Weber (Delano's Domain), trainweb, en.wikipedia and american-rails say scheduled service ended 1 Dec 1931 on loss of the Nanty Glo/Rexis mail contract, with the motor car then running only as needed into the late 1930s. The research report judges 1931 more likely, but 1926-1931 is not drawn on secondary sources a third contradicts; extend to 1931 only on a primary source (Johnstown Tribune or Ebensburg Mountaineer-Herald, June 1925 / Dec 1931; PA PSC order). Headway is an estimate from trainweb's "three round trips a day" (Weber's late timetable also shows three Rexis departures, 8:25 and 10:30 am and 7:35 pm); no headway was counted from a timetable. Freight continued on the Rexis Branch to the July 1977 flood and on the main line to 1994 - context only, not drawn.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 18.59 mi against 18.7 mi documented Colver - Manver (1942 C&I employee timetable; Fowler table 374 gives Colver Heights - Manver 20.9, i.e. 18.7 from Colver). All on C&I-tagged OpenStreetMap ways; no straight-line legs; waypoints Regan Jct, Elkdale Jct and Stiles Crossing on the line, Kinter Crossing 0.2 km off. Colver - Elkdale Jct (5.42 mi) shares geometry with the Colver - Rexis feature. Endpoints: Colver as in that feature; Manver has no OSM place node, so the line ends at the north end of the C&I-tagged grade (40.6497,-78.9258) where its wye legs meet the former Cherry Tree & Dixonville - the documented 18.7 mi agrees with ending there. LATER-ALIGNMENT NOTE: the drawn line is the grade as abandoned (Manver - Glory Crossing lifted 1980s, the rest 1995); no realignment since 1916 is known, but none was checked against an era map.

segments.note: ANCHOR YEAR - one single proven year. Fowler's table 374 letters every station Colver Heights - Manver "a" (Regan Jct, Dobson/Elkdale Jct, Adams, Klines, Stiles, Kinter, Carlson, Sides, Greismore, Glory, Pine Flats, Manver), and the C&I legend reads "a: 1916t" = a 1916 company public timetable. Service certainly ran wider both ways - trainweb says that initially one round trip a day, often a mixed train, ran Colver - Manver, from c.1911-1912 - but no other year is confirmed, and no source dates its end (Weber's later account names only Rexis - Colver, which suggests but does not prove it had ended by the 1920s). Do not widen without a dated source. Headway is an estimate from trainweb's "one round trip a day"; not counted from a timetable. Beyond Manver the Cherry Tree & Dixonville was a joint PRR/NYC property and its trains are not C&I. Freight continued to the 1980s/1994 - context only.
